newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey extends nuclear plant tender bid deadline.
newsitem.headline: Turkey extends nuclear plant tender bid deadline.

text.p: Turkey extended the deadline for bids in its nuclear power plant tender by two months after a request from a participating consortiom, state Anatolian news agency said.
It quoted Ugur Dogan, energy ministry under secretary, as saying that the deadline was extended to end-August from end-June for the tender, expected to cost around $2.5 billion.
"Two participant consortia said they could prepare their bids by June 30. But the third consortium asked for an extension," he said. He did not say which group asked for more time.
Turkey plans the plant near Akkuyu in the southern Mersin province on the Mediterranean coast.
The consortia expected to bid include the following:
--Canadian AECL, Kvaerner John Brown, Hitachi, Turkey's Guris, Gama and Bayindir.
--NPI (A French-German joint company), Siemens, Framatome, GEC -Alsthom, Campenon Bernard, Hochtief, Turkey's Garanti-Koza, Simko, STFA and Tekfen.
The energy ministry meets regularly with the interested consortia to brief them on the progress of the tender.

The project envisages two options for the construction of the power plant, which will be the first such plant in Turkey and has been criticised by local residents, some politicians and environmentalist activists.

The first is a plant of one or more units with a capacity ranging from 900 MegaWatts (MW) to 1,400 MW. The other option's range is between 2,4000 MW to 2,800 MW. Each power production unit in both options should have a capacity of 600 MW or more.
The plant will be fully financed by the builder on a turnkey basis, according to the tender terms.
